title.narrative: Improvement of Solid Waste Management in Dheisheh Camp and the Surrounding Area

description.narrative: This project will improve the Solid Waste Management system of Dheisheh refugee camp as well as in the buffer area (i.e. Doha municipality) through a number of actions that enhance efficiency and streamline collection and processing processes without increasing the financial burden on UNRWA, but rather possibly reducing the overall costs in the future. The duration of the Contirbution Agreement project, implemented by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), is for a period of 3 years (36 months) for an overall budget of EUR 2 million. The project document relies on previous studies and preliminary assessments commissioned by the Office of the European Union Representative (West Bank & Gaza Strip, UNRWA) in Jerusalem, with a number of adaptations to the post-COVID-19 context that include, among others, an updated baseline assessment.

comment.narrative: The workshops and meetings for the validation of the current situation and the definition of the new solid waste management plan were postponed to Year 2. The participatory approach foresaw initial bilateral meetings and a validation workshop.Challenges and remedial actionBased on the information provided in the narrative progress report some delays are foreseen due enforced movement restrictions including the closure of checkpoints and blocked entrances to towns and cities in the area. As a result local project staff faced access restrictions to the target area leading to a number of delays in certain project activities. To address this issue the PMU decided to implement remote working for staff members who could not reach the camp which may result in delays.Inperson meetings workshops and validation sessions with stakeholders were also postponed or rescheduled due to the conflict situation and movement constraints. While remote meetings were scheduled as an alternative the postponement of facetoface interactions may lead to delays in the participatory processes and validation workshops planned for Year 2 of the project.The war in the Gaza Strip since October 2023 has had a subdued impact on the projects activities in the West Bank. A protracted tense situation accompanied with strict closures and access restrictions may have implications for the project timeline and implementation potentially causing delays in planned events and activities.Operational AssessmentOverall Year 1 of implementation was meant as a startup year for the project. These activities have laid the groundwork for the project. AICS signed the grant with the selected implementing organization CESVI in June 2023 providing only a few monthstime for implementation irrespective of the war in Gaza. The first progress report by CESVI is expected to be received by AICS in August 2024. Once the report is made available further details regarding the outputs and results will become clearer. Activities that were originally foreseen for Year 1 but are now taking place in Year 2 mainly include workshops and meetings for data validation and strategic planning. The workshops and meetings for data validation regarding the current Solid Waste Management SWM system including gaps and the definition of the new solid waste management plan have been postponed to the beginning of Year 2 due to the ongoing situation. A number of activities trainings communication and procurement depend on the agreement of all stakeholders including local authority on the new solid waste management plan Strategic Plan for SWM that includes the definition of a new collection system with roles duties ME plan community accountability mechanisms and incentives for workers. This plan is meant to be jointly designed and endorsed by competent authorities for their respective engagement and commitment. While the PMU has taken measures to mitigate delays such as implementing remote working and rescheduling activities external factors and operational challenges mentioned in the report indicate the possibility of delays in certain project activities. It is therefore essential for AICS and CESVI to continue their close monitoring of the situation adjusting timelines as needed and proactively addressing any delays to ensure the successful implementation of the project. A midterm review and audit will also be carried out in Year 2. The EUREP will therefore remain in close contact with AICS to provide guidance and anticipate any warranted amendments or extensions to the contract as already reported by AICS on p. 4 of the narrative report as a possibility.

comment.narrative: The workshops and meetings for the validation of the current situation and the definition of the new solid waste management plan were postponed to Year 2. The participatory approach foresaw initial bilateral meetings and a validation workshop.Challenges and remedial actionBased on the information provided in the narrative progress report some delays are foreseen due enforced movement restrictions including the closure of checkpoints and blocked entrances to towns and cities in the area. As a result local project staff faced access restrictions to the target area leading to a number of delays in certain project activities. To address this issue the PMU decided to implement remote working for staff members who could not reach the camp which may result in delays.Inperson meetings workshops and validation sessions with stakeholders were also postponed or rescheduled due to the conflict situation and movement constraints. While remote meetings were scheduled as an alternative the postponement of facetoface interactions may lead to delays in the participatory processes and validation workshops planned for Year 2 of the project.The war in the Gaza Strip since October 2023 has had a subdued impact on the projects activities in the West Bank. A protracted tense situation accompanied with strict closures and access restrictions may have implications for the project timeline and implementation potentially causing delays in planned events and activities.Operational AssessmentOverall Year 1 of implementation was meant as a startup year for the project. These activities have laid the groundwork for the project. AICS signed the grant with the selected implementing organization CESVI in June 2023 providing only a few monthstime for implementation irrespective of the war in Gaza. The first progress report by CESVI is expected to be received by AICS in August 2024. Once the report is made available further details regarding the outputs and results will become clearer. Activities that were originally foreseen for Year 1 but are now taking place in Year 2 mainly include workshops and meetings for data validation and strategic planning. The workshops and meetings for data validation regarding the current Solid Waste Management SWM system including gaps and the definition of the new solid waste management plan have been postponed to the beginning of Year 2 due to the ongoing situation. A number of activities trainings communication and procurement depend on the agreement of all stakeholders including local authority on the new solid waste management plan Strategic Plan for SWM that includes the definition of a new collection system with roles duties ME plan community accountability mechanisms and incentives for workers. This plan is meant to be jointly designed and endorsed by competent authorities for their respective engagement and commitment. While the PMU has taken measures to mitigate delays such as implementing remote working and rescheduling activities external factors and operational challenges mentioned in the report indicate the possibility of delays in certain project activities. It is therefore essential for AICS and CESVI to continue their close monitoring of the situation adjusting timelines as needed and proactively addressing any delays to ensure the successful implementation of the project. A midterm review and audit will also be carried out in Year 2. The EUREP will therefore remain in close contact with AICS to provide guidance and anticipate any warranted amendments or extensions to the contract as already reported by AICS on p. 4 of the narrative report as a possibility.

However validation is necessary by the project steering commitee.Challenges and remedial actionBased on the information provided in the narrative progress report some delays are foreseen due enforced movement restrictions including the closure of checkpoints and blocked entrances to towns and cities in the area. As a result local project staff faced access restrictions to the target area leading to a number of delays in certain project activities. To address this issue the PMU decided to implement remote working for staff members who could not reach the camp which may result in delays.Inperson meetings workshops and validation sessions with stakeholders were also postponed or rescheduled due to the conflict situation and movement constraints. While remote meetings were scheduled as an alternative the postponement of facetoface interactions may lead to delays in the participatory processes and validation workshops planned for Year 2 of the project.The war in the Gaza Strip since October 2023 has had a subdued impact on the projects activities in the West Bank. A protracted tense situation accompanied with strict closures and access restrictions may have implications for the project timeline and implementation potentially causing delays in planned events and activities.Operational AssessmentOverall Year 1 of implementation was meant as a startup year for the project. These activities have laid the groundwork for the project. AICS signed the grant with the selected implementing organization CESVI in June 2023 providing only a few monthstime for implementation irrespective of the war in Gaza. The first progress report by CESVI is expected to be received by AICS in August 2024. Once the report is made available further details regarding the outputs and results will become clearer. Activities that were originally foreseen for Year 1 but are now taking place in Year 2 mainly include workshops and meetings for data validation and strategic planning. The workshops and meetings for data validation regarding the current Solid Waste Management SWM system including gaps and the definition of the new solid waste management plan have been postponed to the beginning of Year 2 due to the ongoing situation. A number of activities trainings communication and procurement depend on the agreement of all stakeholders including local authority on the new solid waste management plan Strategic Plan for SWM that includes the definition of a new collection system with roles duties ME plan community accountability mechanisms and incentives for workers. This plan is meant to be jointly designed and endorsed by competent authorities for their respective engagement and commitment. While the PMU has taken measures to mitigate delays such as implementing remote working and rescheduling activities external factors and operational challenges mentioned in the report indicate the possibility of delays in certain project activities. It is therefore essential for AICS and CESVI to continue their close monitoring of the situation adjusting timelines as needed and proactively addressing any delays to ensure the successful implementation of the project. A midterm review and audit will also be carried out in Year 2. The EUREP will therefore remain in close contact with AICS to provide guidance and anticipate any warranted amendments or extensions to the contract as already reported by AICS on p. 4 of the narrative report as a possibility.

However validation is necessary by the project steering commitee.Challenges and remedial actionBased on the information provided in the narrative progress report some delays are foreseen due enforced movement restrictions including the closure of checkpoints and blocked entrances to towns and cities in the area. As a result local project staff faced access restrictions to the target area leading to a number of delays in certain project activities. To address this issue the PMU decided to implement remote working for staff members who could not reach the camp which may result in delays.Inperson meetings workshops and validation sessions with stakeholders were also postponed or rescheduled due to the conflict situation and movement constraints. While remote meetings were scheduled as an alternative the postponement of facetoface interactions may lead to delays in the participatory processes and validation workshops planned for Year 2 of the project.The war in the Gaza Strip since October 2023 has had a subdued impact on the projects activities in the West Bank. A protracted tense situation accompanied with strict closures and access restrictions may have implications for the project timeline and implementation potentially causing delays in planned events and activities.Operational AssessmentOverall Year 1 of implementation was meant as a startup year for the project. These activities have laid the groundwork for the project. AICS signed the grant with the selected implementing organization CESVI in June 2023 providing only a few monthstime for implementation irrespective of the war in Gaza. The first progress report by CESVI is expected to be received by AICS in August 2024. Once the report is made available further details regarding the outputs and results will become clearer. Activities that were originally foreseen for Year 1 but are now taking place in Year 2 mainly include workshops and meetings for data validation and strategic planning. The workshops and meetings for data validation regarding the current Solid Waste Management SWM system including gaps and the definition of the new solid waste management plan have been postponed to the beginning of Year 2 due to the ongoing situation. A number of activities trainings communication and procurement depend on the agreement of all stakeholders including local authority on the new solid waste management plan Strategic Plan for SWM that includes the definition of a new collection system with roles duties ME plan community accountability mechanisms and incentives for workers. This plan is meant to be jointly designed and endorsed by competent authorities for their respective engagement and commitment. While the PMU has taken measures to mitigate delays such as implementing remote working and rescheduling activities external factors and operational challenges mentioned in the report indicate the possibility of delays in certain project activities. It is therefore essential for AICS and CESVI to continue their close monitoring of the situation adjusting timelines as needed and proactively addressing any delays to ensure the successful implementation of the project. A midterm review and audit will also be carried out in Year 2. The EUREP will therefore remain in close contact with AICS to provide guidance and anticipate any warranted amendments or extensions to the contract as already reported by AICS on p. 4 of the narrative report as a possibility.
